comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C40-C42 regarding cTBS-induced BOLD signal decreases during semantic tasks. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED with no methodological concerns raised.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C36-C38 regarding cTBS-induced GABA increases. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval additionally references C34, C35, C39 for convergent evidence and control conditions.

Agreement on claims C5, C43-C44 regarding correlation between GABA and BOLD changes. Both find evidence SUPPORTED and acknowledge this as a novel contribution. Peer review also includes C6, C68 in this evaluation, recognizing the mechanistic link claim.

Agreement on claims C31-C32, C57, C59-C60 regarding GABA-performance correlations as replication of prior work. Both find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C7, C58 and notes correlational limitations; peer review includes C61 and emphasizes replication value.

Disagreement on inverted-U relationship claims C9, C62-C64. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with cautious interpretation, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging data sufficiency and raising concerns about practice effects influencing Figure 4D.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for responder/non-responder analysis (claims C51-C53). Both identify methodological concerns: OpenEval cites circular analysis and post-hoc categorization issues; peer review raises 'double dipping problem' that undermines statistical validity.

Partial disagreement on behavioral findings C48-C50. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED despite marginally significant interaction; peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to practice effect concerns that complicate interpretation.

Both address inverted-U model extension to plasticity (C65-C66). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to circular analysis concerns in responder categorization; peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, challenging the inverted-U relationship itself as having incomplete support.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for interpretive claims C10-C11 about individual variability explanations. Both note dependence on questionable inverted-U model; peer review emphasizes incomplete support for underlying relationship.

Divergent evaluations of practice effects (C45). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for task-specific effects; peer review incorporates this into broader UNCERTAIN evaluation, stating practice effect controls were insufficient.

Both address mechanistic claims C6, C68 about GABA mediating cTBS effects. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes correlational limitations on causality; peer review rates SUPPORTED and emphasizes novelty of the GABA-BOLD change correlation.

Both address group comparison claims C55-C56 between responders/non-responders. OpenEval rates overall responder analysis UNCERTAIN; peer review specifically questions validity of these group comparisons due to double dipping in the grouping methodology.
OpenEval includes control finding C39 (no Glx changes) as part of SUPPORTED evaluation showing specificity; peer review separately notes this negative control finding as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both address explanatory framework claims C93-C94. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to post-hoc responder categorization; peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to fundamental double dipping methodological concerns.

Both address claim C95 about inverted-U model extension. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to circular analysis and categorization assumptions; peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to incomplete support for underlying inverted-U relationship.
